items.title: Pay demanded 'Abschlag' instalment to new account
items.quote: Bitte überweisen Sie den fälligen Abschlag von 214,00 € bis spätestens 11.09.2026.
items.computation: The letter states a fixed calendar date, 11.09.2026 (a Friday, not a weekend day or a public holiday in NW), so no weekend/holiday shift applies; as this is a company (not an authority), no deemed-delivery rule applies and the date is taken as written, one business day before which a transfer should be sent to arrive on time. However, this whole letter shows strong hallmarks of a payment-redirection scam (see warnings) — do not actually pay to the IBAN given without independently verifying it with Stadtwerke Musterstadt through contact details you already have.

warnings: This letter has strong hallmarks of a bank-details/phishing scam: it asks payment to be redirected to a new IBAN held by 'Global Energy Payments s.r.o.', a company name completely unrelated to the sender 'Stadtwerke Musterstadt' — legitimate utilities do not change to a differently-named foreign payee overnight.
The IBAN printed (DE61 2004 1111 0512 3456 78) fails its own checksum validation, i.e. it is not even a correctly formed German IBAN — a strong sign of fabrication.

The letter combines extreme urgency (payment due only 4 days after the letter's date) with a threat to cut off electricity 'ohne weitere Ankündigung' (without further warning) — classic pressure tactics used in scams to prevent the recipient from checking.

It explicitly instructs the recipient not to reply in writing and to call only a given mobile number (0157...) instead of the utility's normal customer-service channels — another common scam pattern to route victims to fraudsters and away from verification.
The reply/sender e-mail address 'stadtwerke-musterstadt@kundenservice-mail.example' does not look like an official Stadtwerke domain.

Recommendation: do not transfer any money to the IBAN given in this letter; verify the request directly with Stadtwerke Musterstadt using contact details obtained independently (e.g. a prior bill or their official website), and consider reporting the letter as attempted fraud.
